Notes to Authors

It the policy of this Journal to publish articles in English in all fields of ISLAM provided they are of a high caliber and contribute to the fundamental knowledge of the religion. In keeping with the universal nature of Islam, this journal is not intended to reflect any political, regional, or nationalistic bias. Articles containing unwarranted attacks, direct or implied, against any other religion, sect, belief, or ideology, shall not be accepted for publication. The journal's sole objective is to work within the framework of ISLAM towards a full appreciation of God's message to all humanity.

The journal recognizes the sources of Islamic knowledge to be the Qur'an, the Sunna, analogy (Qiyās), consensus (Ijmā'), and personal thought (Ijtihād). However, THE QUR'AN shall be the ultimate reference. Only statements in full agreement with the Qur'an shall represent the journal's official stand. All other statements, or statements subject to various interpretations shall represent only the author's personal viewpoint.

Manuscripts submitted for publication should be typed, double spaced. Only one copy is required. All Qur'anic quotations must be accompanied by the number(s) of sura(s), and the number(s) of verse(s). Colons should separate the number of sura from the number(s) of verse(s) (e.g. 17:28-33). A group of verses from the same sura should be separated from each other by commas (e.g. 17:28-33, 51, 60-62). When more than one sura are involved, a semi-colon should separate the different suras (e.g. 17:28-33, 51, 60-62; 23:16; 36:9-11, 19-25, 44). The journal will undertake to add the Arabic text to all Qur'anic translations. This is to avoid the inadvertent mental re-translation to an Arabic composition which is different from the original.

Every Hadīth should be accompanied by its sources (transmitters) and the reference book where it may be found. If the transmitter(s) and/or the reference book were not known, this should be stated clearly.

Say, "If the ocean were an ink-well for the words of my Lord, the ocean would run out before the words of my Lord run out, even if twice as much ink were provided."
(Qur'an 18:109)

In the 1975 issue of ISLAM, Volume 1, Numbers 3 & 4, the text discusses the 2 suras Al-Kahf (The Cave) and Maryam. It mentions that the 2 suras are unique in their mathematical structure. It was noted that the 2 suras are mathematically related to the number 19. The text also mentions that the 2 suras are unique in that they are the only ones that contain the letter Qaf (No. 19) in their initial letters. The text discusses the writing of the Quran and the mathematical structure of the suras. It mentions that the letter Qaf has a numerical value of 100, but in the context of the 19-based system, the letter Qaf is used to represent the number 19. The text also mentions that we will look at the sura Al-Kahf and the sura Maryam to state the mathematical structure and the number 19.

We look at the suras at His command. The total number of the verses in the 2 suras and the initial letters are related to the number 19 (19 x 50). It is noted that the total number of verses is 950 (19 x 50).

pages.transcription_text:
Yūsuf Amīn Wālī, Ph.D.

ERRATUM
God’s Message to Humanity:
The Ultimate Proof of Authenticity

In the last issue of ISLAM [1(2): 91-104], it was pointed out that the only 2 suras in the Qur’an which are initialed with the letter Qāf ق [namely, sura Al-Shūrā (No. 42) and sura Qāf (No. 50)] contain exactly the same number of this letter, i.e. 57; that the total number of occurrences of this letter in the 2 suras is 114, the same as the total number of suras in the Qur’an. It was pointed out that this deliberate design and the knowledge of the mathematical distribution of individual alphabets throughout the Qur’an are unattainable by man; that only Allah could have such capability. Allah (the most glorified, most high) placed the initial Qāf at the beginning of the 2 suras to indicate to us His knowledge of the alphabetical distribution; that there is something special about the letter Qāf in these particular suras; that only He is the author of the Qur’an.

On page 98 of that article, however, it was pointed out that sura Ibrāhīm (No. 14) is the only other sura where the letter Qāf occurs 57 times. I am writing this erratum to state that, in comparing the number of occurrences of the letter Qāf, I have overlooked the fact that while suras Al-Shūrā & Qāf have the letter Qāf prefixed to them, sura Ibrāhīm is not initialed with the letter Qāf. If the letter Qāf is prefixed as an initial in sura Ibrāhīm, for a fair and accurate comparison, then the number of occurrences of the letter Qāf will become 58, not the same as the 2 Qāf-initialed suras. To look at it at another way, if we remove all the Qur’anic initials from the Qur’an, we will find that sura Qāf and sura Al-Shūrā contain 56 Qāfs each, while sura Ibrāhīm contains 57 Qāfs. It was neither fair, nor accurate, therefor, to state that sura Ibrāhīm was “the only other sura which contains the same number of Qāfs as the Qāf-initialed suras.”

We can easily envision that Allah (the most glorified, most high) looked at His complete message to humanity, the Qur’an, before the placement of the Qur’anic initials and knew that only two suras qualify to receive the initial Qāf so that the total number of Qāfs in them would equal the total number of suras. These two suras were Al-Shūrā (No. 42) and Qāf (No. 50). In order to give us a signal or a hint that He alone knows the alphabetical

THE ITALIAN "BARNABAS"

According to Church historians, the Gospel of Barnabas does not exist as a complete manuscript, but survives only in fragments and certain ecclesiastical writings of the first and second centuries of the Christian Era. It was written in Greek. It is extremely difficult to find a copy of what exists, either in Greek or in translation. But there does exist another book, a complete manuscript, which calls itself the "Gospel of Barnabas". Allegedly, it was written in Hebrew when it was discovered by Pope Sixtus V (1585-1590 CE), who is said to have translated it from Hebrew into Italian. This Italian "Barnabas" later found its way into the Hofbiblyothek at Vienna, and was translated into English in 1907 by Lonsdale and Laura Ragg. Strangely, the Italian edition has Arabic footnotes.3

The Italian "Barnabas" could not have been written by a disciple of Jesus Christ in the first century C.E. This is the judgment of Christian scholars who have read "Barnabas" and it is one in which this Muslim reader will have to concur. To be sure, it mentions the blessed prophet Muhammad by name, but this presents the first problem. "Barnabas" mentions Muhammad by name much too often for a Christian Gospel. In fact, "Barnabas" mentions Muhammad by name more often than the Qur'an does. At the same time, it contains doctrines which are not approved by either orthodox Christian or Muslim tradition. A chief example of this is the assertion by "Barnabas" that Jesus is not the Messiah and that Jesus cursed Peter for calling him the Messiah.4 By contrast, the Qur'an makes several references to Al-Masīḥ, Īsā b. Maryam, "The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary." There is no disagreement between Islam and Christianity on this point.

For a book supposedly written in Hebrew originally, "Barnabas" uses defective Hebrew in transliteration. Jesus reportedly raises his "eyes to heaven (saying): 'O Elohim Sabaoth, have mercy upon thy servants.'" (p. 21) This construction "Elohim Sabaoth" (God of Hosts) is Greek, not Hebrew. The correct Hebrew form would be Elohei Sabaoth or Elohei has-sabaoth.5 On page 34, "Barnabas" records that "Jesus went to Jerusalem, near unto the Senofegia, a feast of our nation." If this were originally a Hebrew book, the correct term would be Sukkoth, not Senofegia. The reference is to the Feast of Tabernacles, which is Hag has-sukkoth in the Hebrew Bible (Deuteronomy 16:13; Zachariah 14:16, etc.), and skenopegia in New Testament Greek (John 7:2). The reading in "Barnabas", Senofegia, is a Latin form, which points up something very disturbing about this book.

Much of Barnabas shows a dependence on the Latin Bible, rather than the Hebrew Scriptures or the Greek New Testament. For example, in quoting Psalm 50, "Barnabas" writes verses 13 and 14 first and then joins part of verse 12 at the end, making the sense different from that of the 166 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)

Hebrew Bible.6 Many of its quotations from the Old Testament follow the Latin Bible rather than the Hebrew.7 Since the Latin (Vulgate) Bible was not published until 382 C.E., “Barnabas” could not quote from it during the time of Jesus. The dependence on the Vulgate proves that “Barnabas” could have been written not earlier than 350 years after the mission of Jesus!

“Barnabas” quotes from the Old Testament apocryphal book called Susanna (p. 60) which was in the Vulgate, but not in the Hebrew canon. And if the book were written by the Barnabas of the first century, it would never have carried the serious blunder found on page 76 of the English edition. Here “Barnabas” says: “The passover drew near, wherefore Jesus, which his disciples, went up to Jerusalem. And he went to the pool called ‘Probatica’.” “Probatica” was not the name of the pool! The name of the pool was Bethesda (“House of Mercy” in Hebrew) or Bethzatha (“House of the Olive”), according to some manuscripts. The name of the pool seems to have been connected with the miracles which were said to have taken place there, as “Barnabas” admits: “And the bath (pool) was so called because the angel of God every day troubled the water, and whosoever ever entered the water after its movement was cured of every kind of infirmity.” (p. 76, cf. John 5:2-4). However, this explanation of the name Bethesda is not included in the earliest manuscripts of the New Testament and some modern translations omit it. It is thus the more curious that “Barnabas” includes a portion of the New Testament which is based on later manuscripts and then misinterprets its meaning!) “Probatica”, which “Barnabas” mistakes for the name of the pool, is really the name for the sheep-gate which was near the pool. “Probatica” is the Latin form of the Greek New Testament word probatika at John 5:2, meaning “Sheep Gate”. How could a book written originally in Hebrew overlook the very Hebrew name of the miraculous pool, Bethesda, and put in its place a word of Greek derivation which referred, not to the pool at all, but to its gate?

The Italian “Barnabas” is full of fables. Unlike the Qur’an, which insists upon making no distinctions between the prophets, “Barnabas” portrays Muḥammad (peace be upon him) in an almost Divine light, setting him over and above all the rest to a fabulous degree. The passage which Muslims like to quote wherein Jesus foretells the coming of Muḥammad, having denied the Messiahship to Jesus, gives it to the Prophet: “Jesus answered: ‘The name of the Messiah is Admirable (Muḥammad).’” (p. 113) But Muḥammad (peace be upon him) never claimed to be the Messiah, nor does the Qur’an say that Jesus foretold the coming of a Messiah, but of another rasūl. Therefore, even this oft-used verse of “Barnabas” has a fatal flaw.

“Barnabas” could not have been written before the fourth century C.E. and there is evidence that it was written even much later, somewhere in Medieval

times. Two things point to this. First, there was a nominally Muslim group of that period which denied that Jesus was the Messiah, just as "Barnabas" does. Second. on page 96, "Barnabas" refers to the Jewish festival of the Jubilee: "Jesus answered: 'I am indeed sent to the house of Israel as a prophet of salvation; but after me shall come the Messiah, sent of God to all the world; for whom God hath made the world (i.e., Muhammad) . . . and that year of Jubilees, which now cometh every hundred years, shall by the Messiah be reduced to every year in every place.'" Here "Barnabas" again denies the messiahship to Jesus and gives it to Muhammad, but he also speaks of the Jubilee "which now cometh every hundred years . . ." at the time of the disciple Barnabas, the Jubilee came every fifty years! The Jubilee which "now cometh every hundred years" could only refer to the Papal Jubilee of the Catholic Church, which was inaugurated in 1300 C.E. and reduced to 50 years in 1350 C.E. This pinpoints the writing of "Barnabas" as between 1300 and 1350 C.E., some 14 centuries after the mission of Jesus!

The conclusion must be that the Italian "Barnabas" was a purposely fabricated book, written or re-written by someone familiar with Islam but outside of the orthodox (Sunni) tradition of Islam. It could not possibly be the work of the disciple Barnabas, nor is it the fragmentary Gospel of Barnabas whose existence is acknowledged by Chrisitan scholars. Because it contains dogmas and fables which conflict with the Qur'an, it is not really useful to Muslims. Nor do Muslims need it.

Though some Muslims have formed a liking for the Italian "Barnabas," its lack of authenticity makes it useless. As Pope Shenuda III has wisely written, "No where in the Qur'an does it mention . . . 'the gospel of Barnabas.'" The name Barnabas does not appear anywhere in the Qur'an. Furthermore, many of the doctrines contained in this 'gospel' are clearly contradictory to the teachings of Islam."8 The disciple Barnabas of the Bible was not even an eyewitness to the mission of Jesus, though this claim is made in the Italian "Barnabas", where his name is placed in the list of the 12 disciples. None of the Gospels of the Bible has Barnabas in the list, nor do they even mention him. We first meet Barnabas in the Book of Acts (4:34), where he is a helper in Paul's missionary work, "a good man full of the holy spirit and faith." If Barnabas has written a Gospel, it would be similarly an honest and faithful narrative of the life of Jesus, worthy of at least much honor by Chrisitans as the letters of Paul in the Bible, since Paul was not an eyewitness to the ministry of jesus either. But this myth-filled Italian manuscript is not the Gospel of Barnabas. Muslims must look for the real one.

Both words may be represented simply as P-R-KL-TOS, which contains the letters they have in common. The reading PERIKLYTOS must have some manuscript basis, and it could not be incidental that a mere variant of the word found at John 14 and 16 makes P-R-KL-TOS the Greek form of "Muḥammad". The Church interpretation of the P-R-KL-TOS as the Holy Ghost is challenged by some Christian scholars on the basis of certain New Testament manuscripts. Jesus spoke Syriac (Aramaic) and the old Syriac manuscripts of John differ from the standard version of John 14:26 which reads: ". . . the P-R-KL-TOS, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send . . ." These manuscripts in the language of Jesus say simply ". . . the P-R-KL-TOS, the spirit, whom the Father will send."9 "Spirit" carries the connotation also of "inspired person." Therefore, the original meaning of John 14:26 was probably: "Muḥammad, the Inspired One whom the Lord will send . . ." In this respect, John 14:26, which is the only verse in the whole Bible which identifies the P-R-KL-TOS as "the Holy Ghost" is seen to mean something else, and there is thus no verse in the entire Bible which makes such an identification. A study of the Greek New Testament meanings behind John 14 and 16 reveal that they portray the coming of another Messenger, a human being like Jesus, an inspired prophet of God, the Truthful One, Muhammad (P-R-KL-TOS).10

Properly understood, the Gospel of John makes the same point that the Qur'an does at Sūrah al-Ṣaff (61:6):

The Muslims and Jerusalem

The Second Islamic Summit, held in Lahore 22-24 February 1974, having considered the present situation in the Middle East, declared that Jerusalem is a unique symbol of the confluence of Islam with the sacred divine religions. For more than 1300 years, Muslims have held Jerusalem as a trust for all who vernerate it. Muslims alone could be its loving and impartial custodians for the simple reason that Muslims alone believe in all the three prophetic religions rooted in Jerusalem.

The Kings, Heads of States and Governments and the Representatives of the Islamic countries and organizations proclaimed that no agreement, protocol or understanding which postulates the continuance of Israeli occupation of the Holy Arab City of Jerusalem or its transfer to any non-Arab sovereignty or makes it the subject of bargaining or concessions will be acceptable to the Islamic countries. They decided that Israeli withdrawal from Jerusalem should be a paramount and unchangeable prerequisite for lasting peace in the Middle East.

The plain fact is that Jerusalem, the ancient capital of Palestine, enjoys the unique status of a Holy City for the three major world faiths, Islam, Christianity and Judaism. For the Arabs and Muslims, it is enough to recall that, according to the Qur'an, it was from Jerusalem that the Prophet Muḥammad (peace be upon him) began his famous nocturnal journey to

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4): 173-175 173

THE MUSLIMS AND JERUSALEM

Heaven. This, was the place where the Prophet led the congregational prayer with all the Prophets. It is well to recall Jerusalem is regarded as the spiritual home of the Muslims next to Mecca and Medina. In the early days of Islam, it served as the first Qibla of the Muslims, for they used to pray towards Jerusalem when Muhammad still lived in Mecca. After the Prophet migrated to Medina, he continued to pray towards Jerusalem for 16 months, until he was directed to face towards Mecca.1,2

The Dome of the Rock stands on one of the most sacred spots in the world. It was built by Umayyad Caliph Abd al-Malik Ibn Marwan in 961 A.D. on the same site where Caliph ‘Umar built his mosque of wood. The monument is of such noble beauty that it stands unrivalled in the real of sacred art. It is one of the two oldest and most impressive specimens of the early Muslim architecture, the other being the Grand Mosque of Damscuss which has remained intact to this day. The temple area or the Haram al-Shar-if, as it is called by the Arabs, has always been a place of great sanctity for the Muslims all over the world.

Jerusalem was captured by the Crusaders under Godfrey of Bouillon in July, 1099 A.D. who converted the mosque into a church and renamed it Templum Domini. They even built an altar on the Rock. But Sultan Salahuddin, in October, 1187 A.D., recaptured it.3,4,5

After the death of the Sultan, Jerusalem remained under Muslim rule for 731 years. It was ruled in turn by the Ayubites, Mamlukes and finally the Ottomans until 1918, when it was captured by the British forces led by General Allenby.

Indeed, The policy of toleration of the Christians in Muslim countries for a period of thirteen centuries is unique.

Even in 1948, instead of being told that they had been kept for centuries as custodians of the Church, the Christians and therefor the Muslims were denied access.

During the period when they had free access to the holy places, Zionists were fighting a declared state of war between them and those visiting Jerusalem.

Islam & The Third International Theory

IN THE NAME OF GOD

In a world where man is confused whether capitalism or communism offers the values of life, a third path is needed.

Life on earth, which was intended to be so in the beginning of the created world, is now wandering in a maze, to set aside spiritual values and to live in a whirlpool of material life, conscious or unconscious of the ultimate end.

State policies, based on capitalism and materialism, have made that humans are subjected to misery and a complete loss of their identity, even for a few moments of peace.

In olden days, there were no such theories. Only under the Almighty's shade, man knew the true meaning of God on earth, and there were no the veils on the truth that held sway.

Physical life was simple, even when conflict existed, such as in serfdom with the concentration of power as the main objective of men working to improve their inter-human relations, even before the pre-industrial age and the discovery of the machine.

The Creator has freed mankind from true slavery and the heavy bonds for the sake of humanity.

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)

The "Third International Theory" is not a new theory but has been purposely called so for it, partly, screens out the drawbacks of the other two theories now in practice in the world, namely, capitalism and communism, and, partly, because it urges Mankind for a return to God by adopting a third path, different from the two existing ones.

Islam & World Governments:
The Third International Theory

IN THE NAME OF ALLAH, THE MOST COMPASSIONATE, MOST MERCIFUL

In a world where tensions and conflicts abound and in which materialism, whether capitalist or communist, is blinding human beings from the spiritual values of life, a comeback to religion is now gaining momentum.

Life on earth, being as it is, a preparation for the hereafter has stopped to be so in the absence of a genuine religious drive. Man, all through the world, is now working as if he were to exist on earth forever. He has ostensibly set aside spiritual values, the result of which is that he is drifting away in a whirlpool of materialistic values. God, apparently, is being deliberately or unconsciously forgotten . . .

State policies, in their turn, are simply inspired nowadays by mundane and materialistic objectives. Social and economic interrelations among humans are subsequently suffering. Man, today, is groping his way towards complete loss sacrificing his age-old spiritual security and happiness for some few moments of satisfaction he succeeds to snatch every now and then.

In olden times when religion was supreme, there were no man-made theories. Only religion — the divine theory — predominated, and in its shade, man knew happiness and security for he duly felt he was the successor of God on earth. However, human self-conceit and other factors have put the veils on our eyes. Serfdom at one time, was institutionalized and gained sway.

Physical force was instrumental to subdue the freeborn individual and, when conflict of interests increased among the masters, they agreed to replace serfdom with the feudal system. Riches on the earth became the instruments of power as the feudal lords possessed not only the land but also the lives of men working within the confines of this property. In the meantime inter-human exploitation spread in the cities, at first, in a limited way, during the pre-industrial Revolution Age, and, then world-wide after James Watt’s discovery of steam.

The Church, too, had its part in exploiting Man, and flagrantly digressing from true Christianity in the era of the Borgias, began to sell indulgence bonds for the remission of temporal and especially purgatorial punishment.

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4): 177-182 177
pages.arabic_text: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ

pages.transcription_text:
THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY

Clergymen, in the Age of Decadence, were notorious feudal lords, who committed abuses of power as well as other forms of exploitation. Protestantism, a movement which caused a schism within the church, failed to reform the clergy who kept digressing from true Christianity. The Inquisition era is also a salient -digression from Christian tolerance.

Islam, Judaism and even the other non-heavenly creeds have also passed through their own setbacks. But, Islam, for one, has suffered no distortions in its Holy Book though there is a general consensus that some Muslims have had their abuses which caused gross injury to Muslims at large. However, Judaism had been flagrantly distorted to suit the purposes of Zionism. The distortions, it is noted, occurred in the Bible and in the Gospels while, in Islam, only the misbehaviour of some Muslims is detected. (see this issue).

Screening back the evolution of history, it is found that theoricians like David Ricardo and Adam Smith, began to interpret life in terms of capitalist thinking. Of course, Man tried to revolt against exploitation. Theoretically, humanitarian thinkers, philosophers and economists, like St. Simon, Owen, Lasalle and Proudhon appeared and, tried, in their own way, to establish a utopian society of their own. Practically, however, a true mass revolution took place in the year 1789 in France, calling for Liberty, Fraternity and Equality, but this outburst was short-lived as France reverted to militarism to spread its empire.

The communist theory emerged in the year 1848 in a manifesto entirely based on dialectical materialism, which maintains that the basis of reality is constantly changing in a dialectical process giving the priority of matter over mind and metaphysics. This ideology was aimed, in fact, to be against inter-human exploitation but it appeared to be a theory that disregards spiritual values and leaves Man erring astray.

Be all that as it is, the First of September Revolution in the Libyan Arab Republic feels it is its duty to remind Mankind of the necessity for a comeback to God. For humanity, as a whole, is now in dire need for a new path which is to take us back to our religions and to God who created us to be His successors on earth.

The “Third International Theory” is not a new theory but has been purposely called so for it, partly, screens out the drawbacks of the other two theories now in practice in the world, namely, capitalism and communism, and, partly, because it urges Mankind for a return to God by adopting a third path, different from the two existing ones.

From the beginning, it should be said that the Third International Theory is not a theory in the literal sense of the word, nor are its dimensions yet shaped in the Libyan Arab Republic to enable it to answer Man’s

178

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)

Mu'ammar Al-Qadhāfi

day-to-day questions.

However, it is the path of truth. It is not man-made as it is based on religion and, on the divine concept of Islam, specifically. It is not like the common theory liable to change by revocation or change. However, peoples look at the truth from different angles but, truth, in itself, remains always one, immortal and unchangeable because it is a transcendent fundamental and spiritual reality. Therefore, the “Third Theory” is not the exclusive property of any particular nation for it is not expounded for the benefit of a specific group. It is not also a kind of philosophical or ideological thinking for, unlike philosophy and ideology, it does not stop at political limits, the limits of nations and peoples.

In this theory, a humanitarian concept for the seventies and the years to come is being expounded. One aspect of this concept is the enunciation of a firm belief in the reality of existence and its dynamics. Many famous thinkers and philosophers sought for this reality but failed to find it. The reality of existence is not a riddle or a problem to all believers in religion who admit that they are part of that existence, and, being so, cannot transcend to comprehend the intricacies of existence which is a whole, partially closed before the eyes of individual parts.

God, The Creator of the Universie, is the super-human and supra-national deity. He has revealed Himself to us through one religion, namely Islam, In fact, Prophet Muḥammad was not the bearer of Islam for Islam, in the divine concept, existed long before him. Other heavenly messages preceded Muḥammad's message, they had their prophets too also entrusted with messages calling humanity to the path of truth.

But, at one time, the peoples of the earth got confused and thought that Muḥammad's message was Islam. Henceforth, they distinguished themselves as Muslims, while the followers of Jesus-Christ called themselves Chrisitans and the followers of Moses Jews.

That distinction bred contempt and enmity among the followers of the various heavenly messages which all emerge from Allah and are, therefore, Islam proper.

To explain this, in clear-cut terms, we have to dwell on a human interpretation of the divine concept of Islam. This interpretation adopts the following logic:—

1. If all three monotheistic religions emerge from one God, is it then reasonable that these messages contradict with themselves. Of course, there should be no contradictions since the source is one. Therefore, unity exists among all three heavenly messages and this unity in truth is an indisputable reality.

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 179

THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY

2. However, since all three heavenly messages emerge from one source, why then did they not come all at one and the same time? — Man, being weak by nature, always succumbs to lusts and temptations, and, consequently, lacks wisdom and determination. God being all-loving for His creatures, decided to forward to them more than one prophet to guide them to the right path, the path of truth. Whenever humanity digressed, God forwarded one of his prophets to bring Mankind back to reason and to the one true religion. Moreover, Man, being unable to absorb God's teachings in one dose, needed to be reminded intermittently by God's prophets of the one and only message of truth.
3. Why did God consent to Islam being the only religion for His creatures? — Because Islam is the last heavenly religion which completes the two previous ones.
4. Islam is the seal of all other religions and Muhammad is the last of the prophets. This is because the Holy Qur'an came out as a detailed constitution for Man's spiritual and temporal life.

Meanwhile, misinterpretation of the divine concept leads the Jews, for instance, to consider themselves God's “chosen people”. This man-made interpretation, is erroneous for it is based on an egotistic principle entitling the Jews to acquire everything for them and deprive all non-Jews from what is good.

Such being the case, the Third International Theory is based on Islam, in its divine and non-fanatical concept. Religion, it is noted, is the most vital necessity for Man without which he would simply err in life. Even the atheist who seems unaware of religion has a religion of his own. The communist, outside his official work, may be a fervent or a non-fervent Orthodox.

But, religion is humanly conceived in a dual way: a correct conception and a deviationist one. In its correct sense, religion is submission to divine guidance which organizes the relation of Man with his God, with other men and with himself. If conceived from this angle, happiness will prevail over the world and in the hereafter.

on the other hand, religion, in its deviationist sense, is a mixture of feelings, including cruelty, fanaticism, materialism, selfishness and submission to natural phenomena.

The Third International Theory adheres to the correct conception of religion and believes in the universality of Islam as it is a religion that provides answers to every minute question whether it is earthly or spiritual.

Therefore, the Third Theory is the only path capable of uprooting falsehood as it is based on morals, ideals and values. It is also capable of

180

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)

Mu'ammar Al-Qadhāfi

putting an end to man's slavery to materialistic objectives as it considers all men God's creatures, all being equal, gaining preference only through piety.

The Libyan Arab republic is dedicating itself to the benefit of truth, freedom and peace in the world. It does not simply raise this slogan but puts it is implementation. The nationalism it practices is not at all aggressive because a quick look at its development programmes on the home front will promptly divert you from reaching such a naive conclusion. It is assiduously trying to establish bridges of confidence among members of Mankind, and towards this end, it is actively helping all its brothers in humanity to get rid of oppression and colonialism. If it succeeds to base its relations on mutual confidence, and ascertain the integrity of its intentions, beliefs, initiatives, attitudes, as well as the solidity of the ground on which we stand, the 1st of September Revolution will play the role of a catalyst in promoting worldwide efforts to surmount the obstacles created by the materilistic look, by governments and by worldly politics and sophistications.

The Theory it expounds is a humanitarian and not an aggressive theory because Arab nationalism, on which it rests, is not at all agressive as it does not survive at the expense of others. However, adepts of this Theory cannot trust a non-religious man because the latter is not bound to any moral value that will make him stick to a principle or an agreement.

The only interpretation of history accepted by the adepts of the Third Theory is only based on both religion and nationalism. God has created us and scattered us into different nations in order to get acquainted with each other and not to fight and quarrel with each other. None of us can do without these two paramount factors, which, if used properly, can help us solve our problems. True believers in God cannot attack other peoples, rob them of their freedom and enslave them, for this is inequity which cannot be committed by men who fear God. But those who went astray and, deliberately or unconsciously, abandoned religion, have no such consideration. To them might is right. Big powers attack other countries or milk their resources dry in disregard of any ethical obligations.

As for the economic aspects of the Third Theory, we may say that it seeks solutions for Man's economic problems in true socialism.

Socialism, in that sense, is not at all communism, nor is it, in fact, another naming for it. Islam provides for the realization of social justice and equity. It does not give the right to any rich person to use his wealth as an instrument of oppression. Limitation of property means, in Islam, that whenever oppression resulting from excessive wealth arises, the State becomes entitled to curb it, whether through expropriation, nationalization, progressive income tax or any other suitable measures. However, property

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 181

THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY

may continue to be free if it causes no harm. But wealth and property should not be allowed to co-exist in one society. In such a case, the Government is entitled to enact relevant laws which would provide for taking away from the rich to give to the poor, likewise the Third Theory stands against exploiting capitalism. The capitalists in the United States induce their government to create areas of tension so they can find an opening to market U.S. manufactured weapons and keep the warface machinery in operation.

Women in both the East and West have been employed in jobs against their human nature to earn money. Many other forms of exploitation has subdued man and turned him away from God.

Anxiety among the Northern societies (both East and West) leads Man to commit suicide. Suicide in Southern societies (majorly third World countries) is uncommon. Drugs and alcoholic drinks though harmful to Man are being increasingly used in societies which have, deliberately or unconsciously, abandoned religion.

Here, in the Libyan Arab republic, a popular and cultural revolution is now under way. It is an extension of the 1st September Revolution of 1969. Three years were necessary to pave the way before the day when the masses take over genuine power in their hands.

In Libya, a new and pioneering experience is being nation-wide launched. In each village, oasis, city, school, university or organization, People's Committees have been set up.

These committees entitle the masses to govern themselves by themselves and start a veritable change. The popular revolution is, in fact, an operation which consists of destroying everything harmful and untrue, and building anew a society which adheres to the principles of the Third International Theory and to the tasks and objectives set forth by the 1st of September Revolution.

All misleading and dubious thoughts, imported from both East and West, reactionary thoughts and all obstructionist elements are being wiped out.

Only the thought which emerges from Islam, which is a true expression of Arabism, humanitarianism, socialism and progress, should prevail. All those who look down at the people, owing to their positions or grades, are being trampled underfoot in an unbloody purge.

Freedom is being enjoyed here by the working masses; it is not monopolized by any class or group of people. Exploitation, in all its shades, is nation-wide banned. No place in this society exists for the hypocrite, opportunist, regionalist, separatist or member of a political party.

In that sense, the Libyan Arab Republic is exerting every possible effort to create a model society, abiding by the precepts of Islam and humanitarian and spiritual values.

182

Khurshid Ahmad, Director of The Islamic Foundation, London, United Kingdom

Propagation of Islam:
The Basic Principles

This is the first contribution to this journal by Professor Khurshid Ahmad. Although most readers would be familiar with Professor Ahmad's tireless efforts on behalf of Islam, a brief introduction is in order for the benefit of the general readership. Dr. Ahmad is a former professor of economy at Karachi University and, later, at Lester University (England). He has written a number of books dealing with various Islamic topics, and has served as editor for several Islamic journals. Professor Ahmad is a well-known speaker at Islamic conferences around the globe. In this article, he summarizes his long and valuable experience as propagator of Islam in non-Muslim societies.

Movement is a law of nature. Life itself is symbolized by action, effort and movement. In a world that is ever-changing, one has to move even to remain in the same place. What is true of the world of nature is even more true for the individual and social life of man. Islam is fully cognizant of this situation and provides for the efficient operation of this life-mechanism. A number of provisions have been made to make the principle of movement operative in the socio-moral life of the Community of Islam. Da'wah is one such principle. It constitutes a built-in mechanism that keeps the community as well as the individuals who compose it, active and upright, ensures the moral health of the individual and the community, and acts as a corrective force and a blessing for the whole of mankind.

Da'wah literally means call or invitation. In Islamic terminology it connotes the invitation addressed to mankind by Allah and his prophets to believe in Islam, the true religion, the religion of all prophets. The message of the prophets is universal and this invitation is addressed to all without any discrimination. The only valid differentiation between human beings, according to Islam, is based on their response to this Da'wah: those who believe in it or refuse to accept it.

Islam: Faith, Community or Movement.

All the prophets were raised to convey Islam to their People, and Muhammad

184

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4): 184-191

Khurshid Ahmad

(peace be upon him) is the last of these prophets.1 He presented this divine guidance in its complete and final form.2 He invited the entire human race to follow the path of Allah and has been a mercy and a blessing to them all.3 The mission of the prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was to provide this complete guidance to mankind and to establish a community and a movement to act as its standard-bearer. The Muslim Community has been assigned the same role vis-à-vis the rest of the world as the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was assigned to perform in respect of them.

Thus we appointed you a moderate and moderating Ummah, that you may be witnesses (of Truth) to the people and that the Prophet may be a witness to you.4

The mission of the Prophet has been incorporated into the historical role of the Ummah. This has been achieved through two major factors: the preservation of the Qur'an, which embodies the divine guidance and of the example of the Prophet (peace be upon him); and the assignment of the missionary role to the Ummah as its primary function.5 This responsibility rests on each and every believer and not merely on any one class or group of people. It is the common believer who has been primarily charged with this responsibility, and this is a unique feature of Islam. 6 The moral health of the Muslim Community and of society at large depends on the continuation of these roles and responsibilities.

Da'wah: The Islamic Concept

Islam is the religion for man. It is the embodiment of that code of life, that guidance, which the Creator of the Universe has revealed for the benefit of mankind. Its primary concern is to build correct relationships between God and man as well as among men.7

Faith represents one's commitment to God — a commitment to think, feel and live with the awareness of the Lord, to bring his will into harmony with the Divine Will and to strive to make His will supreme in the world. Islam awakens a new consciousness in man and gives him a new outlook on life. Equipped with this new outlook, he joins a community of faith and participates in a movement, a collective effort, to reconstruct human life and society.8 Islam stands, not for life-denial, but for life-fulfillment. It presents a program for the radical transformation of man and society in

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 185
pages.arabic_text: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطًا لِّتَكُونُوا شُهَدَاءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ عَلَيْكُمْ شَهِيدًا

pages.transcription_text:
PROPAGATION OF ISLAM

the light of the basic concepts of the Unity of God (Tawḥīd) and the equality of all people. It gives an integrated view of man: moral and material, and spiritual and temporal, are welded into an indivisible whole. It refuses to divide life rigidly into the things of this world and those of the next; it regards the two as extensions of one another and invites man to enjoy the best of this world and the best of the hereafter. 9

In our own times the Islamic Da'wah has quite often been presented in ways that leave much to be desired. For a host of reasons, some historical, some otherwise, the system which Muslims had evolved for Da'wah was particularly disrupted over the last two centuries. Whatever partial efforts were made to restore some kind of a system remained of limited effectiveness. The rise of Imperialist powers and their political sway over most of the Muslim lands dealt a severe blow to the old arrangement. Christian missions, and later on Communist onslaughts provoked some reaction. However, these efforts mostly were directed to meet specific challenges. Consequently, they not only remained (basically) negative, but also became over-obsessed with the issues raised by these foreign intruders. This distorted the perspective.

It is therefore, necessary that the concept of Da'wah, as it emerges from the Qur'an and Sunnah should be clearly understood.

1. Islam is not the national religion of the Muslim. It is the eternal religion. Muḥammad (peace be upon him) is not the author of Islam. Allāh has revealed essentially the same religion through all His prophets. Thus the prophets Abraham, Isaac, Ismael, David, Joseph, Moses, and Jesus (peace and blessings on them) invited man to follow the path of Islam and no other. 10 The followers of these prophets did not safeguard their teachings with the result that some of the message was lost while in the rest of it the Word of God and the word of man were mixed up. (see insert from the St. Louis Post Dispatch of January 10, 1975).

Muḥammad (peace be upon him) was raised to reveal the same path in its pristine purity and to restore and finalize God's message to all humanity.

The Qur'an is the superceding guardian (Muhaimin) of the doctrine revealed to all the prophets. 11 Muslims believe in all the prophets and we are not allowed to play one off against the other. We invite all people to discover their real religion. The teaching of the Qur'an is to make them eschew all national or racial prejudices and join this universal community of faith. 12 The first principle of Islamic Da'wah is to emphasize this common feature and to ignore all national antagonisms. They are not our concern at all.

186

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)

Khurshid Ahmad

2. Secondly Islam is a complete way of life, and not a scheme of partial reform. It deals with the whole of man, his spiritual, moral, personal and social existence. It offers guidance on every aspect of human life. It aims at spiritual, moral, material and social reconstruction of human society. It tries to change man from within and to enable this new man to create a just and harmonious society. It neither neglects the spiritual, nor the material dimensions of life. The moral ideal of Islam seeks realization in the shape of a God-conscious man operating in a moral society — with its social, economic, political, national and international relations emanating from the basis of truth and justice. It is this complete and integrated view of Islam as a way of life that deserves to be projected in Da'wah.

3. The Islamic Da'wah is to be presented through word and deed at individual and social levels. It is a misconception that Da'wah would be complete or fully effective merely by spreading the knowledge of Islam. The teachings of Islam must be disseminated but this should be accompanied by setting a true Islamic example, individually as well as collectively. The Qur'an emphasizes that a prophet is the first believer;13 he lives according to what he preaches. 14 That is why his words are a source of knowledge and his actions are a model for behavior. 15 Conformity between word and deed, particularly in the context of Da'wah, has been stressed by the Qur'an. 16 It is therefore a fundamental principle that Muslims in making efforts toward Da'wah must also set a good example to the rest of the community. It follows that Da'wah is not merely for non-believers. It is equally important for believers and non-believers; it consists in efforts to Islamise the Muslims17 and to convey Islam to the non-Muslims.

4. Another principle of Da'wah is to carefully examine the circumstances in which the message is being delivered. The message is universal but it should be presented in such a way that its relevance to the situation is fully realized. Moreover, the problems of the society are to be approached in such a way that the evil is atttacked at its roots, not merely at the level of symptoms. This becomes very clear when we try to study in the Qur'an the way in which different prophets conveyed their basic message. All of them tried to go to the root of the problem — whether a people acknowledge the sovereignty of God or not. In the last analysis everything follows from this fundamental outlook. That is why every prophet tried to correct the relationship between God and man. But along with this he took issue with his people in the light of their situation. Prophets Solomon and Moses (peace be upon them) took up the question of magic. Prophet Lūt focused on the sexual morality of his people. Prophet Shu'aib invited them to establish economic justice. Prophet Moses concerned himself with the political and cultural servitude of the Children of Israel.

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)
187

PROPAGATION OF ISLAM

Prophet Joseph looked into the management of the state and its economy. And in respect of each of their problem-areas they showed how the establishment of a proper relationship with God on the correct foundations would help them solve their problems. From this we may infer that the Da'wah should not only take note of the specific problems of the society in which it is being given but should also go deeper and show how a fundamental transformation of outlook is a precondition to the solution of these problems.

5. Da'wah is not merely a system of communication with the outside world, it also includes the evolution of a system of training — of Tarbiyah and Yazkiyah — so that the mechanism for absorption and consolidation should operate along with the machinery for contact and expansion. This is essential for the maintenance and improvement of the moral health of the community itself.

6. The ideal form for Da'wah is that the entire community should be organized on the principle of Khilafah 'ala-Minhaj-al-Nabuwwah (caliphate patterned after the Prophet's life). Under this system the Ummah can attain optimum effectiveness, within and without. The collective system would be a model of Islam. This is the most effective way. But if this is not so, as is the situation today, then on the one hand efforts should be made to establish this system, and on the other, whoever is conscious of the missionary responsibilities of the Ummah should engage in this task individually as well as through organized effort. 18

It is in pursuance of this principle that efforts at Da'wah are being made by muslims in different parts of the world.

7. Another principle is that Da'wah should be presented in a most carefully diplomatic way. The Qur'an says:

Invite others to the way of your Lord with wisdom and gentle admonition and debate with them in the best possible manner. 19

In the Qur'an and Sunnah ample light has been thrown upon certain methodological aspects of Da'wah. Inter alia the following deserve careful consideration.

(i) Those methods should not be used which may inflame the combative passions of the addressees, dim their sense of perception or provoke prejudiced retaliation. 20

(ii) If you are wronged, try to rectify the situation by resorting to good means. "And good and evil are not alike. Repel (evil) with a compassionate response." 21

(iii) The efforts should be... [text continues on right column]

pages.transcription_text:
(iii) The efforts should be made with patience and perseverance. The Qur'anic term for this mode of behaviour is Ṣabr, which implies (a) patience in the sense of being thorough and devoted; (b) constancy, perseverance, steadfastness and firmness of purpose; (c) planned and systematic effort with a realization of phases and grades involved; (d) confidence and belief in the mission itself; (e) a cheerful attitude of acceptance and understanding in sorrow, defeat or suffering and of humble restraint and thankfulness to God in happiness, success and achievement. Ṣabr is the principle of constructive dynamism and of calculated effort in the path of Da'wah.
(iv) To adopt a rational and thoughtful approach and to resort to informed discussion and cool debate. In this respect it is suggested that one should make use of all available knowledge, the most reliable sources.
(v) To be aware of the psychology of the people, their receptivity and responsiveness. Da'wah is not a unilateral process with one way traffic only. It should involve a meaningful dialogue, to be pursued with care, wisdom and patience. The element of time and different quantitative and qualitative consideration should be kept in view.
(vi) The message should be clearly expressed in the language of the people, the crucial importance of the Arabic language not withstanding. This is essential so that they feel at home with the message and are able to follow it.
(vii) Efforts should be made to benefit from the latest and most appropriate techniques of contact and communication. The best possible technology should be used in the service of the Da'wah.
(viii) The process of Da'wah should be properly graduated. We must be clear about our priorities. Fundamentals must have precedence over details. Faith should be the first target. It is only through attainment of faith that the road to Islamic life can be followed. Obligatory duties should come before non-obligatory ones. The objectives and general principles of the Shari'ah should come before its minutia. Sectarian differences should be avoided at all levels and emphasis placed upon the essentials and on the areas of agreement. No effort should be made to achieve everything all at once. The wisdom behind the piece-meal revelation of the Qur'an was that society adopts Islam step by step and gets firmly rooted in it through a gradual process.

PROPAGATION OF ISLAM

Fri., Jan. 10, 1975
ST. LOUIS POST-DISPATCH

Pioneer Reform Judaism Commentary On Torah To Be Published Next Week

By David E. Anderson
UPI Religion Writer

The first volume of a new, liberal commentary on the Torah—the first five books of the Bible—which challenges the view that the Torah is the Word of God will be published next week.

The commentary is the first to be produced by Reform Judaism and the only such work ever published in North America.

Volume 1 of the commentary, which is being published by the Union of American Hebrew Congregations and is expected to be the standard Torah commentary for the nation's 1,100,000 Reform Jews, deals with the book of Genesis. It was written by Rabbi Gunther Plaut of Holy Blossom Temple in Toronto.

"Our commentary disagrees with traditional interpreters over divine origin and mosaic authorship," Plaut said, "But it does agree with them on treating the text as it is, a unified whole for it was approached this way by many generations and, in this way, it has made its impact on history"

Most Orthodox Jews and Fundamentalist Christians believe the books of Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy were written by Moses through direct verbal inspiration from God.

Plaut, however, in his introuctory essay to the commentary, argues that the Torah "is a human book composed by men."

He also argues that it is "A book about man's understanding of an experience with God" and, citing the ancient Jews' oral tradition which resulted in divergent views about God and man, said "these stand side by side in the book and tell us of our ancestors changing and developing beliefs."

"In this sense, then, the book is not by God but by a people . . . it is ancient Israel's distinctive record of its search for God."

Professor M. Farīd Wajdī

ISLAM: Its Mission in the World
3. DECLARATION OF UNIVERSAL BROTHERHOOD OF NATIONS

Of all his achievements as writer, editor of Nour-el-Islam, and Professor at Al-Azhar University, Dr. Wajdi is better known for his famous Qur'anic commentary. This series of articles, which were written by him in Arabic, promises to be a most cherished feature by ALL readers of Islam.

Following the proclamation that it is the true Faith, and the inculcation of the twofold basis of human nature and pure reason on which it was founded, Islam sought to introduce a momentous social reform requisite for a great civilization which The Lord has willed Islam to establish on earth. This momentous reform was the calling of mankind to universal brotherhood. For though Islam did not differ, in its doctrinal principles, from the message revealed to previous Prophets, yet it was favoured by certain circumstances which anterior religions lacked. Intercourse between nations was so difficult that it was well-nigh impossible to bring them all together to one universal religion. This privilege was destined by The Lord to be granted to Islam in whose time intercourse between nations was rendered feasible. The Divine Wisdom has seen fit to afford it all the qualifications and advantages which make it a universal religion fitted for all times and climes.

Was the world then at the advent of Muhammad in need of a violent blow from heaven to urge it to unity, or a wrathful cry from high to stop the misguided in their career of sin and aberration?

We may well leave the answer of this question to a foreigner, the great French orientalist Monsieur Jules Le Baum. In the introduction to his index of the Holy Qur'an, he described the world's conditions prior to the advent of Muhammad in the following terms:
At about the time when Muhammad was born, the world was seething with trouble and unrest.

He then began to detail the generalities of this statement pointing to the animosity and contention which raged fiercely between nations:
The world's atmosphere was charged with fierce vibrations. Evil was more counted upon than good and the minds of men were not at rest. The chiefs who won most of the confidence of the people, were those who raised the strong and made strong nations, cities, lords, mendicants.

Had it not been for some cells of civilization from the raging sea, the apostles of progress and arrogance of the age of savagery.

Had it not been for the small light which flickered in the depths of some cells of cenbites, and for some philosophic principles sheltered from the raging storms and transmitted from soul to soul by the bold apostles of progress, barbarism, accelerated in its march by the arrogance of the masters of brutal force, would have become pure savagery.

After long dwelling on the condition that then prevailed, the writer said:

It was during those sad circumstances, and in that heavily charged atmosphere, that Muhammad Ibn ‘Abdallāh, was born on the 29th of August 570.

Indeed! the Arab nation itself was no less divided and contending than the rest of the world. Through tribal division, it formed a collection of antagonistic communities which knew no peace and were for ever on the war-path. The Arabian Peninsula was a vast battlefield on which all the dictates of love and mercy were completely ignored so much so that a man was to clout his sandal from the very skin of his enemy after having him slain and mutilated.

It was in that chaotic era, in that atmosphere of stygian darkness and ruthlessness, that The Lord bade Muhammad to raise high the standard of universal brotherhood and to establish for mankind the foundation of that unity. The Lord’ saying was thus revealed to him:

The Arabs among whom this high and noble principle was preached, were most proud of lineage and boastful of forefathers. Each tribe claimed the greatest honour for itself in that respect and so much indeed had this tendency been exaggerated among them that they were wont to establish the pedigree of their camels and horses to raise them thereby above all others of their kind. The reader may well imagine their disdain for other distant peoples and tribes differing from them in colour, language and traditions.

This universal brotherhood proclaimed by Islam may well be considered a herald of a new era in the history of nations, and a prelude to further universal Qur'anic principles calculated to achieve the unification of human views and objects.

We could not however leave off this subject without alluding to the beauty of the convincible style in which this great principle, like every other principle preached by the Holy Qur'an, is couched.

The Lord has first called the attention of mankind. unity and peace among men so that they may devote themselves to attain personal and social perfection, then why did it have recourse to war? Why did it seek expansion in neighbouring countries? and why did it flood near and distant people the way it did? Why did it not content itself with evidence and proof in calling those people to its cause? And why did it not seek to win their approval by mere conviction and good example?

Our answer to this objection is that Islam is primarily a religion which conforms to the laws of nature as well as to the social factors governing life. Up to the advent of Islam, those laws and factors required a certain amount of force, otherwise the mission of Islam would have been a failure and no trace would have been left of it.

On account of the open prohibition of war ordained by Christianity it continued in a weak condition for over three hundred years. The Roman Emperors were wont to put to death all its adherents, dismember them while they still lived and hunt them down wherever they went.

When Constantine, whose mother had embraced Christianity, and secretly brought him up as a Christian, came to the throne, he used force to propagate this religion and gave orders to pull down the pagan temples and forced people, under penalty of torture, to embrace it. The ascendancy of Christianity goes back to that date and for the very same reason, it is firmly established up to this day in many parts of the world.

Should Islam have contented itself with preaching without having recourse to force, it would have been restricted within the Peninsula and the unbelievers would have forced its adherents to forsake it.

Even if it were spared annihilation, Islam would have found itself in a similar position as that of the Religion of Abraham which was preached by a few men scattered throughout Arabia of whom no trace could be found among human communities.

But although Islam had prepared for war, yet it had certainly mitigated a great deal of its severity and rendered more humane the laws pertaining to it. A just code was established by Islam which definitely prohibited aggression. (See [Quran 2:190]) Indeed, the greatest merit in favour of Islam is that it did not ordain war for despoiling nations or levying tributes thereon, but it was wielded as a means for the propagation of the word of Allah among nations. Never before had any nation waged war for this reason. Wars were waged to subjugate people, appropriate their wealth and products and finally take full possession of everything in the land.

Yet withal, The Lord had commanded His Prophet to make the universal welfare of men the object of war, and if nations wished for peace one day for any consideration, it is incumbent on him to acquiesce to their demand and to sheathe the sword depending for the propagation of the Faith on

pages.page_title: The Falsification of Hadith: History and Development
pages.transcription_text:
Professor Muhammad ‘Ajjāj Al-Khaṭīb, College of Sharī‘ah (Islamic Law), University of Damascus

The Falsification of Hadith: History and Development

While the Qur’an enjoys the Divine guarantee of God’s own protection and eternal preservation [15:9], the second source of Islamic jurisprudence, namely, the Hadith suffered disastrous human distortion, misinterpretation, falsification, and fabrication. A great number of Hadiths (the Prophet’s sayings and traditions) were rescued and verified through the life-time exertion of such scholars as Al-Bukhārī, Muslim, Abū Dawūd, Al-Tirmidhī, Al-Nasā’ī, Ibn Mājah, and others. However, even within the works of each of these scholars, a significant proportion of questionable Hadiths still exists. In this article, presented in Arabic and in English, Professor Al-Khaṭīb reports on the history and development of fabricated Hadiths; with the hope that the readers may be better able to evaluate the Hadiths they come accross. The ultimate criterion for judging the authenticity of Hadith shall always be the Qur’an, the eternally-protected message of Allah. Any “Hadith” which contradicts any Qur’anic principle(s) should be deemed incorrect.

The traditions of the Prophet Muhammad (Allah’s peace and blessings be upon him) remained pure and free from falsification throughout the reign of the four great caliphs. For as long as the Muslim ummah remained solidly behind their rulers, the Prophet’s sunnah remained unadulterated. Only when people with fanatic political and or materialistic tendencies succeeded in dividing the Muslim ummah that the abuse and downright fabrication of Hadith took place. The first break in the solidarity of the ummah is traceable to the assassination of the third caliph ‘Uthmān (may Allah bestow His pleasure and grace upon him). That tragic event shook up the Muslim ummah so violently, that the damaging consequences still live with us today. Although the ummah was able to re-unite behind the fourth caliph ‘Ali b. Abū Ṭālib (Allah’s pleasure and grace upon him), the events which ensued were much too powerful to permit the continuation of sustained unity. The divisive elements succeeded in breaking the ummah into two major camps; one supporting the caliph and encompassing the people of Ḥijāz (Arabia) and Iraq.

the other supporting Mu'āwiyah b. Abū Sufiān, the viceroy of Syria, and encompassing the people of Syria and Egypt. This disastrous division led to the historical Taḥkīm (judgment between 'Ali and Mu'āwiyah to determine who is worthy of Khilāfah), and to bitter wars between the two feuding factions. The Taḥkīm itself resulted in more division within the ummah: four different groups were formed:
1. The majority of Muslims remained solidly behind the caliph 'Ali, since he was the legitimate, shūra-selected Amīr-ul-Mu'minīn (the caliph selected by general consensus of the leaders and representatives of all Muslims), following the assassination of the third caliph 'Uthmān.
2. The party of Mu'āwiyah which was initially formulated to "avenge the death of 'Uthmān, but ended up demanding the caliphate for their leader Mu'āwiyah. Following the Taḥkīm, this group did capture the caliphate. and Mu'āwiyah became the ruler of the torn ummah.
3. The Khawārij (The Rebels) who were supporters of 'Ali, but rebelled against him for accepting the Taḥkīm; they declared that only Allah had the power of Taḥkīm. At the same time, they violently opposed Mu'āwiyah for wanting to snatch the caliphate away from 'Ali.
4. Following the martyrdom of Amīr-ul-Mu'minīn 'Ali, some of his supporters formed the Shi'ah party and demanded restoration of caliphate to Ahlul Bait ('Ali's family).

The Falsification

Since each one of the above mentioned parties wanted to muster the allegiance of the Muslim ummah, they sought to support their political views by Qur'anic statements and sunnah traditions. Thus, some of them resorted to flagrant misinterpretations of the Qur'an; some even attempted to falsify the Qur'an itself. With the divine guarantee of the Qur'an's integrity, those who attempted to distort the Qur'an were immediately exposed. Too many people had already committed the Qur'an to their memory, and the Qur'an distorters got nowhere. What they succeeded in, however, was the injection of false Ḥadīths into the Prophet's traditions, as well as misinterpreting the existing Ḥadīths. With the passage of time, so many false Ḥadīths were fabricated that the authentic Ḥadīths became almost completely indistinguishable from the false ones. The first falsified Ḥadīths were characterized by the praise and over-glorification of certain individuals, such as the four great caliphs, and Ahlul Bait; something they neither needed nor advocated. Then, other fabrications of Ḥadīths dealt with the establishment of certain political parties and various religious sects. With the appearance of each political group, and various religious sects. With the appearance of each political group, a number of fabricated Ḥadīths showed up supporting the creation of such

The supporters and the opponents both wasted no time in creating the best-sounding Hadiths and attributed them to the most credible sources from among the closest Sahabah (Companions of the Prophet).

The falsification of Hadith during that most unfortunate period in Islamic history expanded to cover almost all aspects of the Muslim’s life, including the rites of worship, the permissions and prohibitions, the praise or criticism of certain localities and times of the year, medical advice, the laws of inheritance, etc.

As for the exact time in history when these ominous falsifications took place, it can be safely stated that they started after the era of Sahabah (the first generation of Muslims). Due to their positive participation in the establishment of Islam, the first generation of Muslims were not easily deceivable by false Hadiths. Imam Ibn Taymiyyah describes the history of falsification as follows:

The Prophet’s companions (peace be upon them) were not as susceptible to deceit by false Hadiths as those of later generations. There is no evidence of Hadith falsification through the reign of ‘Uthman. Upon his assassination, however, two opposing factions emerged within the Muslim ummah; each faction vied for the allegiance of the populace by inventing and falsifying Hadith. These two groups were the Khawarij (the rebels) who called ‘Ali b. Abu Talib a “Kafir = heathen,” and the Shi‘ah who called for the Imamat (spiritual leadership) of ‘Ali, his infallibility, his prophethood, and even his divinity (deification).

Towards the end of the first century (Hijra), and during the reign of Ibn al-Zubair and ‘Abdul-Malik, two more groups emerged, namely, the Murji’ah and the Qadariyyah. Still later, at the beginning of the Tabi‘in (Successors = Second generation of Muslims) era, the Jahmiyyah and the Mushabbihah parties appeared. With the emergence of these groups, the falsification of Hadith intensified; each group seeking to support its own views, and its own leaders. The time when falsification started, therefore, should be tied with the appearance of these and other political parties. It is highly improbable that any falsification at all took place during the era of Sahabah. Certainly, it is not expected that the Sahabah who were so devoted to the Prophet that they willingly gave up their properties, their comfort, their homes, and even their lives in defense of the Prophet’s mission, would fabricate lies and attribute them to their beloved leader. The majority of falsified Ḥadīths were fabricated in Iraq, where most of the violent political turmoil materialized into open bitter wars, and where the seeds of religious rift were sown. Iraq became so famous for fabricating Ḥadīth that it became known as “The Mint;” Ḥadīth was coined there like Dirhams. In Medina, meanwhile, Imam Mālik advised the Muslims, “Look on the Ḥadīth of the Iraqis the way you look on the Ḥadīth of the people of the scripture (Jews and Christian); neither believe, nor disbelieve them.” ‘Abdul-Raḥmān b. Mahdī once told Mālik, “During my 40-day visit to Medina, I learned only 400 Ḥadīths; Back home in Iraq, we hear this same number of Ḥadīths in one day.” Imam Mālik replied, “In Iraq you have ‘The Mint;’ you coin Ḥadīth during the night, and spend during the day.” Another reflection on the Iraqi fabrication of Ḥadīth is recorded in the remark by Ibn Shihāb that “The Ḥadīth which leaves Medina only on Shibr (10 inches) long, comes back from Iraq one Dhirā‘ (one yard) long.”

Why Were the Ḥadīths Fabricated?

As mentioned above, the major reasons for Ḥadīth fabrication were the attempts of newly emerging political parties or religious groups to muster maximum support from the populace. The assissination of ‘Uthmān was the triggering mechanism of this disasterous turn of events. The reasons for fabrication, however, increased progressively with time as detailed below:
1. Influence of the Political Parties: The first party to emerge immediately after the assassination of ‘Uthmān was the Shī‘ah party; supporters of the caliph ‘Ali. The second party, Al-Khawārij (opponents of ‘Ali) appeared only after the battle of Ṣiffīn.
(a.) The Influence of Shī‘ah:
In his explanation of Nahjul-Balāghah (the well-known collection of speeches attributed to ‘Ali b. Abu Ṭālib), Ibn Abul-Ḥadīd said, “The origin of falsified Ḥadīth can be traced to the Shī‘ah; they wanted to increase the loyalty and devotion to Ahlul-Bait by fabricating a number of Ḥadīths praising certain individuals. When their opponents, those who supported the four great caliphs, saw the fabrications of the Shī‘ah, they countered by yet fabricating their own set of Ḥadīths praising the caliph Abu Bakr.” Eventually, the enemies of Islam took advantage of this unfortunate situation and planted the seeds of hatred

THE FALSIFICATION OF HADITH

through fabrication of outrageous Hadiths which praised Ahlul-Bait beyond all reasonable levels, and/or cursed the great caliphs Abu Bakr, ‘Umar, and ‘Uthman, beyond all reasonable limits. These falsifications served only to inflame the feelings of these opposing factions of the Muslim ummah, and led to the tragedies and disastrous wars the victims of which were the Prophet’s own grand children and great grand children (the children and grand children of ‘Ali). History recorded the gruesome and heart-breaking tragedies which resulted from blind hatred and victimized but the beloved Ahlul-Bait (may Allah bestow His pleasure and grace upon all of them). Ironically, it was the exaggerated praise and over-glorification of Ahlul-Bait imbedded in false Hadiths that led to such tragedies; praise and over-glorification which Ahlul-Bait neither called for, nor needed. Certainly, it is not possible that Ahlul-Bait like Al-Hasan, Al-Husain, Muhammad b. Al-Hanafiyyah, Ja‘far Al-Sadiq, or Zeid b. ‘Ali would falsify the Hadiths fabricated by the Shi‘ah were innumerable; as their groups increased, so did their fabrications and distortions of existing Hadith. They falsifying, and misinterpreting Hadith, thus hurting their own beloved Imam ‘Ali (may Allah bestow His grace and pleasure upon him) more than benefiting him. Abul-Faraj b. Al-Juzi comments on this situation by saying, “The laudable characteristics of Amir-ul-Mu’minin ‘Ali were innumerable, but his Shi‘ah were not content; they fabricated what actually lowers, rather than elevates their leader.” ‘Amir Al-Sha‘bi wrote, “No one in this ummah had more lies narrated about him than ‘Ali (Allah’s pleasure and grace be upon him).”

The Hadiths fabricated by the Shi‘ah were innumerable; as their groups increased, so did their fabrications and distortions of existing Hadith. They fabricated Hadiths praising ‘Ali (Allah’s grace and pleasure be upon him), as well as Hadiths downgrading Mu‘awiyah and the Umayyads. In the Following sections, examples of the Shi‘ah-fabricated Hadiths and the response of their opponents are given: Since the Shi‘ah wanted first to establish the Prophet’s will that ‘Ali was “his favorite successor,” they wrote a number of Hadiths to support their wishes. Among such false Hadiths is one which states, “The bearer of my will, the depository of my secrets, the successor in my family, and the best one to succeed me is ‘Ali.” Also, “O‘Ali, I designate you as a prophet, though there shall be no prophets after me.” Also, “For each prophet there is a will-bearer, and inheritor; my will-bearer and inheritor is ‘Ali b. Abu Talib.” Also, “When the Prophet (Allah’s peace and blessings be upon him) was raised to heaven on the night of Isra’ and Mi’raj, Allah showed him the marvels of each heaven. On the

Unfortunately, some non-Shī‘ah became incensed by the attacks against Abu Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Uthmān, and Mu‘āwiyah, and decided to fabricate some Ḥadīths highly praising these great Ṣaḥābah and “exonerating” them. The examples of fabricated Ḥadīth given above all represent the

To make matters worse, some good-intentioned Muslims saw what the opposing parties have done to the honorable Ṣaḥābah, and, induced by their desire to exonerate the Ṣaḥābah and nullify the effect of false Ḥadīths against them, they too began to fabricate their own group of Ḥadīths. They sought to show that all four caliphs are equal, that all Muslims shall equally love, respect, and honor all four of them. This group of fabricators thought that they were performing a service; that they were enhancing conciliation between the warring factions. Examples of their fabrications include a Ḥadīth stating, "Allah has commanded me to treat Abu Bakr as a father, 'Umar as a consultant, 'Uthman as a supporter, and 'Ali as a close ally. You are four; Allah has made a covenant with you in the preserved scripture; whoever loves you shall be a pious believer; whoever hates you, shall be only a guilty hypocrite; you shall be the successors after me, and the executors of my will." Also, "A caller will call on the Day of Resurrection, 'Where are the companions of Muhammad?' and Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthmān, and 'Ali will be brought forth." Also, "Whoever curses Al-Ṣiddīq shall be wicked; whoever curses 'Umar shall be destined to Hell; whoever curses 'Uthman feuds with Al-Raḥmān; whoever curses 'Ali feuds with the Prophet (Allah's blessings and peace be upon him)."

When we look at the fabrications of all these groups, we find that the vast majority of fabrications were done by the Shī'ah group.

(b) The Influence of Al-Khawārij:

We do not find in the available references any evidence that the Khawārij resorted to fabrication of Ḥadīth to support their argument. The only hint of possible falsification by the Khawārij is the narration by Ibn Luhay'ah that he heard a former member of Khawārij say, "You should exercise extreme care when you look at any Ḥadīth; when we liked anything, we used to make up a Ḥadīth for it." However, we find no record of any Khawārij-manufactured Ḥadīth among the fabricated Ḥadīths. Additionally, the person Ibn Luhay'ah referred to remains unknown. If anything, there is plenty of evidence that the Khawārij considered lying a gross sin, and a characteristic of the disbelievers. Thus, although the Khawārij were in gross error when they opposed Amīrul-Mu'minīn 'Ali, and contributed but divisiveness to the Muslim ummah, it is unlikely that they falsified Ḥadīth.
