pages.transcription_text: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا وَأَصْلَحُوا وَبَيَّنُوا فَأُولَئِكَ أَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَنَا التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ ﴿١٦٠﴾ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَمَاتُوا وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ ﴿١٦١﴾ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا لَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ الْعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ ﴿١٦٢﴾ وَإِلَهُكُمْ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الرَّحْمَنُ الرَّحِيمُ ﴿١٦٣﴾ إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَالْفُلْكِ الَّتِي تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِمَا يَنْفَعُ النَّاسَ وَمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِنْ مَاءٍ فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ وَالسَّحَابِ الْمُسَخَّرِ بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَآيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ ﴿١٦٤﴾ وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَتَّخِذُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَنْدَادًا يُحِبُّونَهُمْ كَحُبِّ اللَّهِ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَشَدُّ حُبًّا لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ يَرَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا إِذْ يَرَوْنَ الْعَذَابَ أَنَّ الْقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعَذَابِ ﴿١٦٥﴾ إِذْ تَبَرَّأَ الَّذِينَ اتُّبِعُوا مِنَ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوا وَرَأَوُا الْعَذَابَ وَتَقَطَّعَتْ بِهِمُ الْأَسْبَابُ ﴿١٦٦﴾ وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوا لَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةً فَنَتَبَرَّأَ مِنْهُمْ كَمَا تَبَرَّءُوا مِنَّا كَذَلِكَ يُرِيهِمُ اللَّهُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ حَسَرَاتٍ عَلَيْهِمْ وَمَا هُمْ بِخَارِجِينَ مِنَ النَّارِ ﴿١٦٧﴾

SURA AL-BAQARAH
2:172-180
(Prohibited Meats)
172 O you who believe, eat from the good things We provided for you, and be thankful to Allāh if you sincerely worship Him.
173 He only prohibits for you the meat of dead animals, the blood, the meat of swine, and the meat which is dedicated to other than Allāh. However, if one is forced to eat these, without being malicious or deliberate, commits no sin. Surely, Allāh is Forgiver, most Merciful.
174 Those who conceal what Allāh has revealed in this scripture, and trade it away for a cheap material gain, they eat into their bellies but fire; Allāh will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and they shall suffer a painful punishment.
175 It is they who chose the straying over the guidance, and the punishment over the forgiveness. Therefore, they will have to endure the hellfire.
176 That, because Allāh sent down this scripture bearing the Truth; those who dispute this scripture are in extreme error.
(The Definition of Righteousness)
177 Righteousness is not simply turning your faces towards the East or the West (in ṣalāt); but righteousness is to believe in Allāh, the Last Day, the angels, the scripture, and the prophets, and to donate the money, despite one's love thereof, to the relatives, the poor, the alien, the beggars, and for the liberation of slaves, and to observe the ṣalāt prayers and the Zakāt charity, and to fufill the promises whenever they are made, and to steadfastly persevere in the face of adversity, hardship, and war. These are the truthful; these are the pious.
(The Punishment for Murder)
178 O you who believe, ordained for you herein is commensuration when imposing the maximum punishment for murder; the free person for the free person, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. However, if the guilty is pardoned by the victim's kin, then he shall pay an equitable compensation. This is an alleviation from your Lord and mercy. Whoever transgresses these limits shall suffer a painful retribution.
179 Commensuration shall be a life-saving law for you, O you who possess understanding, that you may achieve piety.
(A Will Shall be Written Before Death)
180 It is ordained for you herein that when death approaches the one of you, if he is to leave any wealth behind, a will shall be made for the sake of the parents and relatives equitably. This is an obligation on those who are pious.

الجزء الثاني (٢) سورة البقرة

يَأَيُّهَا النَّاسُ كُلُوا مِمَّا فِي الْأَرْضِ حَلَالًا طَيِّبًا وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ (١٦٨) إِنَّمَا يَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالسُّوءِ وَالْفَحْشَاءِ وَأَنْ تَقُولُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ (١٦٩) وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّبِعُوا مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ قَالُوا بَلْ نَتَّبِعُ مَا أَلْفَيْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا أَوَلَوْ كَانَ آبَاؤُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ (١٧٠) وَمَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي يَنْعِقُ بِمَا لَا يَسْمَعُ إِلَّا دُعَاءً وَنِدَاءً صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ فَهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ (١٧١) يَأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ وَاشْكُرُوا لِلَّهِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ إِيَّاهُ تَعْبُدُونَ (١٧٢) إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةَ وَالدَّمَ وَلَحْمَ الْخِنْزِيرِ وَمَا أُهِلَّ بِهِ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ بَاغِ وَلَا عَادٍ فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (١٧٣) إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْتُمُونَ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَيَشْتَرُونَ بِهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا أُولَئِكَ مَا يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ إِلَّا النَّارَ وَلَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَلَا يُزَكِّيهِمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (١٧٤) أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ بِالْهُدَى وَالْعَذَابَ بِالْمَغْفِرَةِ فَمَا أَصْبَرَهُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ (١٧٥) ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ نَزَّلَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِي الْكِتَابِ لَفِي شِقَاقٍ بَعِيدٍ (١٧٦)

لَيْسَ الْبِرَّ أَنْ تُوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ قِبَلَ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ وَلَكِنَّ الْبِرَّ مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالْكِتَابِ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ وَآتَى الْمَالَ عَلَى حُبِّهِ ذَوِي الْقُرْبَى وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينَ وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ وَالسَّائِلِينَ وَفِي الرِّقَابِ وَأَقَامَ الصَّلَاةَ وَآتَى الزَّكَاةَ وَالْمُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِهِمْ إِذَا عَاهَدُوا وَالصَّابِرِينَ فِي الْبَأْسَاءِ وَالضَّرَّاءِ وَحِينَ الْبَأْسِ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُتَّقُونَ (١٧٧) يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِصَاصُ فِي الْقَتْلَى الْحُرُّ بِالْحُرِّ وَالْعَبْدُ بِالْعَبْدِ وَالْأُنْثَى بِالْأُنْثَى فَمَنْ عُفِيَ لَهُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ شَيْءٌ فَاتِّبَاعٌ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَأَدَاءٌ إِلَيْهِ بِإِحْسَانٍ ذَلِكَ تَخْفِيفٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ فَمَنِ اعْتَدَى بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَلَهُ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (١٧٨) وَلَكُمْ فِي الْقِصَاصِ حَيَاةٌ يَا أُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ (١٧٩) كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ إِنْ تَرَكَ خَيْراً الْوَصِيَّةُ لِلْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ حَقّاً عَلَى الْمُتَّقِينَ (١٨٠) فَمَنْ بَدَّلَهُ بَعْدَمَا سَمِعَهُ فَإِنَّمَا إِثْمُهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يُبَدِّلُونَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ (١٨١) فَمَنْ خَافَ مِنْ مُوصٍ جَنَفاً أَوْ إِثْماً فَأَصْلَحَ بَيْنَهُمْ فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (١٨٢) يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ (١٨٣) ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 265

pages.arabic_text: أَيَّامًا مَّعْدُودَاتٍ ۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكم مَّرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ فَعِدَّةٌ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ ۚ وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُ فِدْيَةٌ طَعَامُ مِسْكِينٍ ۖ فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيْرًا فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّهُ ۚ وَأَن تَصُومُوا خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ ۖ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ ﴿١٨٤﴾ شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ الَّذِي أُنزِلَ فِيهِ الْقُرْآنُ هُدًى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَاتٍ مِّنَ الْهُدَىٰ وَالْفُرْقَانِ ۚ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ الشَّهْرَ فَلْيَصُمْهُ ۖ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ فَعِدَّةٌ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ ۗ يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ وَلِتُكْمِلُوا الْعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُوا اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَاكُمْ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ ﴿١٨٥﴾ وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ الدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ ۖ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِي وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا بِي لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ ﴿١٨٦﴾ أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِّيَامِ الرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَائِكُمْ ۚ هُنَّ لِبَاسٌ لَّكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ لِبَاسٌ لَّهُنَّ ۗ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ كُنتُمْ تَخْتَانُونَ أَنفُسَكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَعَفَا عَنكُمْ ۖ فَالْآنَ بَاشِرُوهُنَّ وَابْتَغُوا مَا كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ ۚ وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ ۖ ثُمَّ أَتِمُّوا الصِّيَامَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ ۚ وَلَا تُبَاشِرُوهُنَّ وَأَنتُمْ عَاكِفُونَ فِي الْمَسَاجِدِ ۗ تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ فَلَا تَقْرَبُوهَا ۗ كَذَلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ آيَاتِهِ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ ﴿١٨٧﴾

1395/1975: An Historical Year

Praise be to Allāh, Lord of the Universe; the most Compassionate, most Merciful, and may Allāh bestow peace and blessings on His beloved messenger Muḥammad.

The journal ISLAM will not be published during the year 1395/1975 in order to devote all our editorial efforts and full resources and capabilities to the final stage in the production of an historical first, namely, THE FIRST QUR’ANIC TRANSLATION BY A MUSLIM SCHOLAR WHOSE MOTHER TONGUE IS ARABIC. This final stage represents the culmination of many years of painstaking effort and dedicated exertion to produce an English rendering of the Qur’an’s meanings as accurately as humanly possible; a rendering which is worthy of God’s finalized and completed message to all mankind.

Realizing the awesome responsibility inherent in translating and/or interpreting God’s message, the Arab Muslim scholars of the past 1400 years have shied away from this great undertaking. Thus, though it is the ruling constitution in the lives of millions of English-speaking Muslims, the Qur’an was never previously translated into English by a Muslim Arab. The evident errors, inaccuracies, deficiencies, and inconsistencies common to the presently available translations have been a source of frustration and disappointment for the English-speaking students of the Qur’an. In spite of the admirable life-time efforts of such great Muslim scholars as ‘Abdullah Yūsuf ‘Ali and Muḥammad Marmaduke Pickthall, it is no secret that their renderings did not capture the spirit of the

My beloved: Do not argue with others in defense of the truth. All you need to do is declare it. You are not responsible for their rejection of the truth; if they accept it, then Allah has blessed them; if they reject it, you are not liable.
Salāmah b. Ḥasan Al-Rāḍī

Faith is necessary for religions, but it ceases to be so for those who go further and who achieve self-realization in God. Then one no longer believes because one sees. There is no longer any need to believe, when one sees the Truth.
Ahmad b. Muṣṭafā Al-‘Alawī

270

Islamic Concentrates

The Aphorisms
of Salāmah Al-Rāḍī: 3

These aphorisms, with their esoteric connotations, are derived from the Qur'an, the sunna, teachings of the great imams, and the principles of Sufism. Published for the first time in English, these particular aphorisms are valuable pieces of advice delivered by one of the greatest Sufis of all time, Shaykh Salāmah Al-Rāḍī, to his dervishes.

31. My beloved: Once you achieve absolute slavery to Allah, you become masters of your surroundings; you say to anything, "Be," and it is. Once you eliminate your ego, and live totally devoted to your Lord, everything obeys you.

32. My beloved: If you become filled with the love of Allah, all things will go your way: you simply wish for anything, and it comes true.

33. My beloved: Your Master treats you in the like of your treatment of Him; If you remember Him, He remembers you; If you long for Him, He longs for you; If you hasten to please Him, He hastens to please you. Accorkingly, judge your position with Him for yourselves.

34. My beloved: If you care only for your own desires, and fail to control them, you may not be admitted into the court of your Master. Moses had said, "My Lord, how can I reach you?" God said, "Abandon your ego and come."

35. My beloved: Your monies and your children are favors from Allah to you for as long as they do not divert you away from your Master; If you abandon your Master in their favor, they become but a disastrous curse.

36. My beloved: If your hearts are purged from loving anything besides your Master, He grants you a restful worldly life; only a minimum of worldly work will sustain you. Otherwise, you will have a life of hard labor.

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) : 271-275

THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3

37. My beloved: So long as the ego remains alive, the heart remains dead. Therefore, you shall revive your hearts by killing your egos; the heart is the abode of the Lord, most Glorified, most High.

38. My beloved: If you wish to avoid the opposition of anyone, you shall not compete with him for the things he loves.

39. My beloved: If you wish to achieve a high rank, do not claim for yourselves any rank. And, if anyone claims for himself a rank above you, do not dispute him, and allow him such a claim. As a consequence, you will taste the genuine sweetness of Īmān and Allah will fill your hearts with light.

40. My beloved: Whenever anyone transgresses against you, you shall attribute your troubles to your sinful deeds, and see that Allah is the One who punishes you. Do not seek revenge, nor shall you pray to Allah against your enemy. You shall be pardoners, for the beloved Prophet (blessings of Allah and peace be upon him) said, "The pardoners shall be the winners."

41. My beloved: You shall avoid all forms of show-off for it renders your efforts a servitude to other than Allah. Your Master needs not any of your deeds, and when you do anything for the show-off, He will not accept your works, saying, "Take your recompense from whomever you showed off your works."

42. My beloved: Our works are filled with deficiencies and insincerity; they are not worthy of the Almighty. How then can we pride ourselves with that which is defective? We can only turn to Allah in hopeful anticipation that out of His abundant grace, He might accept our works despite the defects therein.

43. My beloved: Directing your attention to the purgation of your hearts is much more important than preoccupying yourselves with the collection of knowledge; Purging your hearts will open the doors of Divine knowledge for you, and the knowledge will come to you in its pristine purity, unadulterated.

44. My beloved: Whenever you speak of anything, you shall speak of the good qualities, rather than the bad qualities thereof. The mentioning of bad qualities is itself a bad quality, and you may become so accustomed to seeing bad qualities that you end up believing that everthing must have bad qualities.

272
ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)

THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3

45. My beloved: Your bodies are vehicles, while your souls are the drivers thereof; Let not the vehicles take you to what angers your Master; they are driven only by your souls.

46. My beloved: The real affliction is to turn away from Allah, and the real disease is that of skeptic hearts. Thus whenever you see such afflictions in others, you shall ask Allah to grant you health, and to alleviate their afflictions.

47. My beloved: Seeking the materials of this world, as a sole objective, leads away from Allah, and results ultimately in spiritual death. Thus, regretting the loss of worldly materials would be like regretting the loss of a poisonous snake.

48. My beloved: Turning away from materialism and towards Allah is the key you need for opening your hearts; when one lacks this key, his heart remains locked.

49. My beloved: This worldly life is an attractive illusion; who ever rejoices over material gains therefrom actually rejoices over that which diverts his heart and takes him away from his Lord.

50. My beloved: When you turn on your physical senses, you simultaneously turn off your spiritual senses; this leads to blindness of the soul. Therefore, you shall strive to open your spiritual eye which sees the Divine dominion, by keeping the physical eye from preoccupation with the worldly dominion.

51. My beloved: The people are of varied qualities, and when you associate yourselves with the evil ones, your souls become adulterated; this in turn leads to spiritual sickness and misery for you.

52. My beloved: If you find sweetness in the taste of everything which emanates from your beloved Master, then you have achieved genuine steadfastness. But if you find some of His givings to be sweet and some to be sour, then this indicates a deficiency in your love. When you taste sourness from the beloved Master, this reflects your objection, and the lack of total submission to Him.

53. My beloved: If you love two entities, your heart would be divided in two; each half would compete with the other for complete dominance. This will at least dim the brightness of your love, and the beloved Master requires pure, undivided, attention.

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)
273

THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3

54. My beloved: The human being is an animal by his body; an angel or a devil by his soul. The wise among you would reflect and judge whether he wants to be an animal, a devil, or a pure angel.

55. My beloved: The capital of each one of you is right here in this world; whoever wastes away his capital, how could he make any profit?

56. My beloved: This worldly life is like the Suq market (operates only on a specific day of the week); if one misses the market, where will he sell his goods?

57. My beloved: However you live in this world, so will be your life in the Hereafter; you shall reflect and determine for yourselves whether your life here is in the blessings and pleasure of Allah, or are you incurring His anger (God forbid)?

58. My beloved: The character of the human being is the garment of his soul; you shall reflect and note whether your soul's garment is clean, pure, and lighted, or dirty, dark, and vile.

59. My beloved: If the one of you is told that a scorpion got into his garment, he would immediately take it off or tear it off to get rid of the scorpion. Inside each one of us we have the various lusts which continue to sting our hearts without invoking a reaction from us.

60. My beloved: The grave is your inevitable abode; you shall strive to make it a spacious, and well-lighted abode. If your present spiritual abode is spacious and well-lighted, so will your graves.

61. My beloved: If you are impressed by good deeds, you should first fetch the sincerity therein; if you do not find it, then discount them as good deeds.

62. My beloved: Your works are but ghosts; their real life and light are in the hearts. If the heart accompanies your good works, they would be of value; otherwise, they will be life-less, light-less.

63. My beloved; If you become too impatient with humbleness, then you should realize that your ego is trying to take you out from the courtship of Allah. Beware lest it succeeds in dismissing you from the Divine courtship.

64. My beloved: Once you become fully content with your Lord, your command becomes His command, and your deeds become solely in His name; nothing will disobey you. If your "self" expresses its own wishes, this

274
ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)

THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3

would reflect a defective heart; then nothing will obey you or go your way.

65. My beloved: If you wish to progress along the path of humbleness, you shall keep company with the people of humbleness until you are genuinely humble on your own. Afterwards, you may mix with all kinds of people. Those who keep company with other than the people of humbleness, before being genuinely humble on their own, will be like one who tries to light a feeble candle in the midst of a violent storm.

66. My beloved: The breath of the human being who is in a state of obedience to Allah is but light, and the light is accompanied by angels; if he is in a sinful state, every breath is but darkness, and the darkness is accompanied by devils. The light emanating from each of you, or the darkness, surrounds you. Thus, look around you and find out whether you are surrounded by light and angels, or darkness and devils.

67. My beloved: As you like the people to treat you, so shall be your treatment of them; what you dislike from the people, let them not see coming from you. He who expects the people to treat him better than he treats them is utterly unjust; he who does what others dislike deserves mal-treatment; he who does things for which he later apologizes may not someday find a valid excuse, and if he does, his excuse may not be accepted.

68. My beloved: Do not argue with others in defense of the truth. All you need to do is declare it. You are not responsible for their rejection of the truth; if they accept it, then Allah has blessed them; if they reject it, you are not liable.

69. My beloved: So long as your hearts are totally devoted to your Master, you continue to reside in His courtship. Once they become fond of anything else, they become deprived of His courtship. You shall watch your hearts very carefully lest they love other than your Master.

70. My beloved: Once you taste the sweetness of Īmān (unshakeable faith), you lose the taste for this worldly life. Any heart which actually enjoys the taste of this life is forbidden from tasting the sweetness of Īmān.

275
ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)

(٤٧) سُورَةُ مُحَمَّدٍ مَدَنِيَّةٌ
الآية ١٣ نزلت في الطريق أثناء الهجرة
وآياتها ٣٨ نزلت بعد الحديد
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ
الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَضَلَّ أَعْمَالَهُمْ ﴿١﴾ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَآمَنُوا بِمَا نُزِّلَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ كَفَّرَ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ وَأَصْلَحَ بَالَهُمْ ﴿٢﴾ ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا اتَّبَعُوا الْبَاطِلَ وَأَنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّبَعُوا الْحَقَّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ كَذَلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ أَمْثَالَهُمْ ﴿٣﴾

IN THE NAME OF GOD, THE COMPASSIONATE, THE MERCIFUL

Those who disbelieve and divert others from the path of Allah, God will render their work but vain. As for those who believe and do good works; those who believe in what was revealed through Muḥammad (for it is the truth from their Lord), God will remit their sins and care for them. That, because those who disbelieve follow but falsehood, while those who believe follow the truth from their Lord. Thus does God set the examples for mankind.
(Qur'an 47:1-3)

276
ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)

The Invocations of ʿAbdullāh Anṣārī : 3

ʿAbdullāh Anṣārī, a famous Persian Sufi, was born in Herat 396 AH (1005 C.E.). It is said that one of his ancestors was a companion of the prophet Muhammad (God's blessings and peace be upon him) who moved to Herat with ʿAṣāf, son of Qays. Anṣārī's father, Abu Manṣūr Muḥammad Anṣārī, became a permanent resident of Herat.
These invocations, translated into English by Sir Jogendra Singh, contain true advice to guide the Pilgrim along the path of discipleship to the temple of peace. They come from a man who himself had trodden the path and found what his heart desired.
When ʿAbdullāh Anṣārī departed from this world, he was 85 years old, leaving behind a wealth of Sufi knowledge. Among his well-known works are Risāla Munājāt (The Book of Prayer), Tabaqat-ul-Ṣūfiyyah (The Book of Sufis), Zād-ul-ʿĀrifīn (Provisions of the Sufi Teachers), and Kitāb-i-Isrār (The Book of Mysteries).

My friend, make an effort,
That thou mayest become a man,
And gather treasures
Of feeling for others,
So that with the favour of saints
And by the blessings of waiting on them
Thy cheeks may grow pale,
And love of the world grow
Cold in thy heart.

If thou wishest to become a man
In the world,
In the path of religion
Learn to feel for others,
Night and day attend on holy men.
When thou hast become like dust
Of their feet
Thou shalt become a man.

277

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) : 277-282

THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3

O man, remember death at all times;
Renounce all discord and tyranny;
Deem what has not been done as done,
And what has been done as not done.
Watch vigilantly the state of
Thine own mind.
Love of God begins in
Harmlessness.

Know that the Prophet built an external Kaba
Of clay and water,
And an inner Kaba in life and heart.
The outer Kaba was built by Abraham,
The Holy;
The inner is sanctified by the glory of
God Himself.

On the path of God
Two places of worship mark the stages.
The material temple,
And the temple of the heart.
Make your best endeavour
To worship at the temple of the heart.

O mendicant, paradise is only an
Allurement;
The real objective is
The house of God Himself.

Fasting only means the saving of bread,
Formal prayer is the business
Of old men and women,
Pilgrimage is a pleasure of the world.
Conquer the heart,
Its subjection is conquest indeed.

If thou canst walk on water
Thou art no better than a straw.
If thou canst fly in air
Thou art no better than a fly.
Conquer thy heart
That thou mayest become somebody.

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)
278

THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3

One man spends seventy years in learning
And fails to kindle the light.
Another, all his life learns nothing
But hears one word
And is consumed by that word.

On this path argument is of no avail;
Seek, and thou mayest find the truth.

Helpless in childhood,
Intoxicated in youth,
And decrepit in old age;
Then, O helpless one, when couldst thou
Worship God?

Alas! alas, for the master-craftman's ways:
From the same iron he forges a horse-shoe
As well as a mirror for the Emperor.

My friend, see thine own faults;
The faults of others,
For thee they are not.
Make thy heart forgiving;
Nor sell thy soul for the fruits of the world.

It is wrong to consider oneself above all others
And to exalt one's self.
Learn from the pupil of thine eye
To see others, but to thyself be blind.

Know friend,
Human sorrow springs from three things:
To want before it is due,
To want more than the destined share,
To want for oneself
What belongs to others.

When Providence has provided thy share
Separately from others
Then why art thou jealous,
And hungering for that which is not for thee?

Desire for knowledge is the path
Of honour;
Desire for wealth, that of dishonour.

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)
279

THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3

Wealth is the chain which slaves wear
Knowledge the kingly crown.

The path is narrow and beset by
Yawning chasms.
Woe to him who is heavily laden with sin
And walks without the light of faith.

He with whom virtue has become a habit,
Hath accomplished his work here,
And hereafter.

The law of life requires:
1. Sincerity to God.
2. Severity to self.
3. Justice to all people.
4. Service to elders.
5. Kindness to the young.
6. Generosity to the poor.
7. Good counsel to friends.
8. Forbearance with enemies.
9. Indifference to fools.
10. Respect to the learned.

Know that four things are symbols of
Ill luck:
Ingratitude in good fortune,
Impatience in ill fortune,
Discontent with what fate ordains,
Hesitation in serving fellow-men.

In this path, be a man
With a heart full of compassion.
Engage not in vain doing,
Make not thy home in the street of lust and desire.

If thou wouldst become a pilgrim on the path
Of love
The first condition is
That thou become as humble as dust
And ashes.

Remove “A” from “Murad” (desire) it becomes
Murd (man);
He who renounceth desire becometh a man.

280

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)

THE INVOCATIONS OF 'ABDULLAH ANSĀRĪ : 3

Know that he who desires the things of the
World
Is haunted by sorrow.
He who desires Heaven
Is a labourer working for wages.
But, he who desires God,
Is on the path of glory.

O thou who covetest the world
How long wilt thou follow the path of sorrow?
Even if thou seekest the pleasures of Heaven
Thy quest is on the wrong trail.
But if thou seekest God and receivest His seal,
Thou art victorious in both the worlds.

Know, that when thou learnest to lose thyself
Thou wilt reach the Beloved.
There is no other secret to be revealed,
And more than this is not known to me.
Be humble and cultivate silence.
If thou hast received, rejoice,
And fill thyself with ecstasy
And if not, continue the demand.

Be a rose and not a thorn!
Be a friend and not an enemy!

To exalt the Beloved is to practise religion;
To exalt the self is to practise paganism.

If the seeker is worthy
Attainment is easy.

The company of a good friend
Is the light of the soul.
The company of an ungodly person
Is the poison of life.
A snake is preferable to a faithless friend.

Were I to abide in fire a hundred
Years
That scorching flame would be easier to bear
Than the company of Godless men;
Death is preferable to such company.

ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)                                                                                                              281

THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3

What is worship?
To realise reality.
What is the sacred law?
To do no evil.
What is reality?
Selflessness.

The heart enquired of the soul
What is the beginning of this business?
What its end, and what its fruit?
The soul answered:
The beginning of it is
The annihilation of self,
Its end faithfulness,
And its fruit immortality.

The heart asked what is annihilation?
What is faithfulness?
What is immortality?

The soul answered:
Freedom from self is annihilation;
Faithfulness is
Fulfilment of love;
Immortality is union of immortal
With mortal.

O Devotee, if thou lovest God truly
Why dost thou cast longing eyes
On things other than Him?

In this path the eye must cease to see,
And the ear to hear.
Save unto Him, and about Him.
Be as dust on His path,
Even the kings of this earth
Make the dust of His feet.
The balm of their eyes.

282
ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)

pages.transcription_text:
Islamic Concentrates
The Islamic Calendar Conversion Table : 3
(Hijra / Gregorian)

Over the first five issues of ISLAM, the Journal will publish this table for convenient conversion of dates from either of the two calendar systems. Such chronological conversion tables have been difficult to find yet most indispensible for the Western scholar of Islam. Since all great works of Islamic literature refer exclusively to Hijra dates, the Editors feel that these tables will be useful to many readers.

According to the historians, the prophet Muḥammad (God's blessings be upon him) arrived at Medina on the 12th day of Rabi‘ I, coincident with September 24, 622 CE (Christian Era). This sets the first day of the first Hijra year (Muharram 1, 1) as July 16, 622. Fifteen hundred Hijra years will be covered in these tables (622-2076 CE).

بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
اللَّهُمَّ بِسَطْوَةِ جَبَرُوتِ قَهْرِكَ وَبِسُرْعَةِ انْتِصَارِكَ لِأَنْبِيَائِكَ وَرُسُلِكَ وَأَوْلِيَائِكَ إِنَّكَ أَبْطَأْتَ غَارَةَ الْأَرْحَامِ وَبَعُدَتْ إِغَانَةُ نَصْرِكَ وَبِغَيْرَتِكَ لِانْتِهَاكِ اللَّهُمَّ انْتَصِرْ لَنَا أَنْصَارَكَ لِأَحْبَابِكَ فَأَقْرَبُ السَّرِيمِ يَا غَارَةَ اللَّهِ
حَرَمَاتِكَ وَبِحِمَايَتِكَ لِمَنْ احْتَمَى عَلَى أَعْدَائِكَ ، اللَّهُمَّ لَا تُمَكِّنِ يَا غَارَةَ اللَّهِ وَجْدَيَ السَّرِيرُ سَرِيعَةً
بِآيَاتِكَ أَمَّا لَكَ يَا اللَّهُ يَا سَمِيعُ الْأَعْدَاءَ فِينَا وَلَا تُسَلِّطْ عَلَيْنَا بِذُنُوبِنَا يَا مَنْ حَلَّ عُقْدَتِنَا يَا غَارَةَ اللَّهِ
يَا قَرِيبُ يَا مُجِيبُ يَا سَرِيعُ يَا مُنْتَقِمُ حَم حَم حَم حَم حَم حَم حَم عَدَتِ الْعَادُونَ وَجَارُوا
يَا شَدِيدَ الْبَطْشِ يَا جَبَّارُ يَا قَهَّارُ يَا مَنْ الْأَمْرُ وَجَاءَ النَّصْرُ فَعَلَيْنَا لَا يُبْصَرُونَ وَرَجَوْنَا اللَّهَ مُجِيرًا
لَا يُعْجِزُهُ قَهْرُ الْجَبَابِرَةِ وَلَا يَعْظُمُ حَمْعَقَ حِمَايَتُنَا مِمَّا نَخَافُ ، اللَّهُمَّ وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ وَلِيًّا
عَلَيْهِ هَلَاكَ الْمُتَحَرِّدَةِ مِنَ الْمُلُوكِ قِنَا شَرَّ الْأَسْوَاءِ وَلَا تَجْعَلْنَا مَحَلًّا وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ نَصِيرًا
وَالْأَكَاسِرَةِ أَنْ تَجْعَلَ كَيْدَهُمْ بِالْبَلْوَاءِ ، اللَّهُمَّ أَعْطِنَا أَمَلَ الرَّجَاءِ حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ
كَادِي فِي نَحْرِهِ وَمَكْرَ مَنْ مَكَرَ وَفَوْقَ الْأَمَلِ يَا هُوَ يَا هُوَ يَا هُوَ حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ
بِي عَائِدًا عَلَيْهِ وَحَفْرَةً مَنْ حَفَرَ يَا مَنْ بِفَضْلِهِ لِفَضْلِكَ نَسْأَلُ - حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ
لِي وَوَاقِعًا فِيهَا وَمَنْ نَصَبَ لِي شَبَكَةَ نَسْأَلُكَ الْعَجْلَ الْعَجْلَ إِلَهِي وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
الْخِدَاعِ اجْعَلْهُ يَا سَيِّدِي مُسَاقًا الْإِجَابَةَ الْإِجَابَةَ يَا مَنْ أَجَابَ نُوحًا الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ اسْتَجِبْ لَنَا
إِلَيْهَا وَمُصَادِفًا فِيهَا وَأَسِيرًا لَدَيْهَا فِي قَوْمِهِ يَا مَنْ نَصَرَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَى آمِينَ
اللَّهُمَّ بِحَقِّ كَهْيعص اكْفِنَامُ الْعِدَا أَعْدَائِهِ يَا مَنْ رَدَّ يُوسُفَ عَلَى يَعْقُوبَ لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
وَلِقَهْرِ الرَّدَى وَاجْعَلْهُمْ لِكُلِّ يَا مَنْ كَشَفَ ضُرَّ أَيُّوبَ يَا مَنْ أَجَابَ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ اسْتَجِبْ لَنَا
حَبِيبٍ فِدًى وَسَلِّطْ عَلَيْهِمْ عَاجِلَ دَعْوَةَ زَكَرِيَّا يَا مَنْ قَبْلَ تَسْبِيحَ آمِينَ
النِّقْمَةِ فِي الْيَوْمِ وَالْغَدِ. اللَّهُمَّ يُوُسَ بْنَ مَتَّى نَسْأَلُكَ بِأَسْرَارِ لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
بَدِّدْ شَمْلَهُمْ ، اللَّهُمَّ فَرِّقْ جَمْعَهُمْ أَصْحَابِ هَذِهِ الدَّعَوَاتِ أَنْ تَقَبَّلَ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ اسْتَجِبْ لَنَا
اللَّهُمَّ أَقْلِلْ عَدَدَهُمْ ، اللَّهُمَّ فَلَّ مَا بِهِ دَعَوْنَاكَ وَأَنْ تُعْطِيَنَا مَا سَأَلْنَاكَ آمِينَ
حَدَّهُمْ ، اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْ الدَّائِرَةَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَنْجِزْ لَنَا وَعْدَكَ الَّذِي وَعَدْتَهُ فَقُطِعَ دَابِرُ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا
اللَّهُمَّ أَرْسِلِ الْعَذَابَ إِلَيْهِمْ ، اللَّهُمَّ لِعِبَادِكَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ لَا إِلَهَ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
أَخْرِجْهُمْ عَنْ دَائِرَةِ الْحِلْمِ وَاسْلُبْهُمْ مَدَدَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ
الْإِمْهَالِ وَغُلَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ وَارْبِطْ عَلَى مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ انْقَطَعَتْ آمَالُنَا وَصَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا
قُلُوبِهِمْ وَلَا تُبْلِغْهُمْ الْآمَالَ ، اللَّهُمَّ وَعِزَّتِكَ لَا أَمِنْكَ وَخَابَ رَجَاؤُنَا مُحَمَّدٍ النَّبِيِّ الْأُمِّيِّ وَعَلَى
مَرَّقْهُمْ كُلَّ تُمَرِّقِ مَرَّقْتَهُ لِأَعْدَائِكَ وَحَقِّكَ لَا أُفِيكَ.
آلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ وَسَلَّمَ

pages.transcription_text:
IN THE NAME OF ALLAH, THE MOST COMPASSIONATE, MOST MERCIFUL

They say, “The Almighty has begotten a son!” Indeed, you have committed a gross error. The heavens almost disintegrate, the earth almost shatters, and the mountains almost crumble, because they attribute a son unto the Almighty. It never befits the Almighty that He begets a son. Everyone in the heavens and the earth is no more than a slave of the Almighty. He has counted as such each and everyone. All shall come to Him on the Day of Resurrection as helpless individuals. As for those who believe and do good works, the Almighty will bestow on them love. Thus, We herein deliver a clear message through your tongue (O Muhammad), that you may convey good news to the righteous ones, and to warn therewith the defiant ones.
(Sura Maryam 19:88-98)
pages.arabic_text: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَٰنُ وَلَدًا ۝ لَقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْئًا إِدًّا ۝ تَكَادُ السَّمَاوَاتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْهُ وَتَنَشَقُّ الْأَرْضُ وَتَخِرُّ الْجِبَالُ هَدًّا ۝ أَنْ دَعَوْا لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ وَلَدًا ۝ وَمَا يَنْبَغِي لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدًا ۝ إِنْ كُلُّ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ إِلَّا آتِي الرَّحْمَٰنِ عَبْدًا ۝ لَقَدْ أَحْصَاهُمْ وَعَدَّهُمْ عَدًّا ۝ وَكُلُّهُمْ آتِيهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فَرْدًا ۝ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ سَيَجْعَلُ لَهُمُ الرَّحْمَٰنُ وُدًّا ۝ فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَاهُ بِلِسَانِكَ لِتُبَشِّرَ بِهِ الْمُتَّقِينَ وَتُنْذِرَ بِهِ قَوْمًا لُدًّا
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
